issue.title: Improve documentation about partial mocks and doReturn() style of stubbing
issue.body:
I think the documentation here is wrong:
https://github.com/mockito/mockito/blob/release/2.x/src/main/java/org/mockito/Mockito.java#L1646 

I believe the doReturn() syntax should be used there instead. At least when I do that it works but when I do the when(myFoo.myMethod()).thenReturn() that line itself runs the real impl of myMethod.

final: {"number": 1262, "label": "docs", "route": "answer", "related": [1492, 1396, 1381], "evidence": ["mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/Mockito.java"], "reply": "Thanks for the report. The current Javadoc in Mockito.java already covers this. The CALLS_REAL_METHODS Javadoc (Note 1) says that when(mock.getSomething()).thenReturn(fakeValue) calls the real method on a partial mock, and recommends doReturn(fakeValue).when(mock).getSomething() instead. The spy() Javadoc in the same file also recommends doReturn for stubbing spies. The line you linked points to the release/2.x branch, which seems to predate this wording. If you still see the old text in a released version, please tell us which version so we can check it. Your observation that when().thenReturn() runs the real method is correct and expected for partial mocks."}
